context: It is also natural to ask for what values of p the random graph G(n, p) is k-vertex-minor universal for n polynomial in k. The main difficulty in extending our approach to p ̸= 1/2 is that the random walk defined in Section 3.1 now has steps which are correlated to each other: after flipping an edge which was not yet revealed, its probability of existing is now 1 − p instead of p. If one could get around this issue, the resulting random walk would then have the second largest eigenvalue bounded in absolute value by the max of 1 − 2p2 , 1 − 2(1 − p)2 , and 1 − 2p(1 − p). Assuming without loss of generality that p ≤ 1/2, this means it would suffice to run the random walk for O(k 2 /p2 ) steps. Thus we conjecture the following. √ ▶ Conjecture 32. If p = ω(1/ n) is at most 1/2 and G ∼ G(n, p) or G ∼ G(n, 1 − p), then √ G is k-vertex-minor universal with high probability for some k = Ω(p n). If true, this would qualitatively generalize Theorem 3, although unlike Theorem 3 it is not necessarily tight up to a constant for all p. Conjecture 32 would also imply that G(n, p) is not a counterexample to Conjecture 9 for any p. This follows for instance by noting that if p is outside the range [n−1/4 , 1 − n−1/4 ], then G(n, p) already contains a clique or independent set of size Ω(n1/4 log n).
